items.title: James "Sing" Miller Interview, 1971-01-17
items.q: The term 'Cook' is used by the interviewer as a generic occupational noun ('the cook cooked him') referring to the person who prepared the chicken, not as a proper name of a specific individual with a personal relationship to the interviewee.

ctx.x: Yeah, they were strange chickens. That's how I, that's how I learned how to kill chicken. We were gonna put that same one out of the restaurant, I'm gonna tell you about it. Oh. People come there and say, give me all that chicken. Go back, get my broomstick and get that chicken right up underneath his cap and dig it. That was it. He couldn't walk anymore so he had to die.
And then you, then the cook cooked him? Cook cooked him, man.
Did you have to clean him up?
